equalTensionDerivation.premises: Standard elementary ideal pulley model: one continuous flexible massless rope, frictionless freely turning massless pulleys, taut load-bearing segments. Current ideal-system context invokes this standard model rather than arbitrary multiple independent ropes.
equalTensionDerivation.reasoning: A massless rope element cannot sustain unequal end tensions; otherwise force would be nonzero on zero mass. A frictionless massless pulley cannot sustain a tension difference/torque. Thus the common continuous rope has uniform T. For n parallel segments supporting the moving load in the load direction, total support is nT; a segment that also routes the pull remains counted if it supports that assembly. A free segment acting only at a fixed redirector adds no direct load support.
equalTensionDerivation.sourceRelation: Yale L35 identifies ideal vs actual/friction distinction; L91 and especially L100 distinguish supporting strands from ONLY-redirecting strands. Uniform tension is mechanics derivation consistent with those premises, not text quoted from Yale. Parallelism is needed for simple additive nT in the support direction, not itself the cause of equal tension.
equalTensionDerivation.limits: Not asserting actual frictional equality, arbitrary angled strand nT, multiple independently tensioned ropes, or accelerating massive rope/pulleys.
